title: Investing in What Matters to People
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Using Crystal Maggelet, CEO of Flying J and Maverik, as a case study, the article argues that leaders build loyalty by investing in what matters most to their people. Her holding company employs over 7,000 mostly hourly workers and has created programs around their children's education, including tutors, payments for good grades and generous tuition reimbursement. The author reads this as a message to employees that they and their children matter, which creates an unusual bond and makes them treat the company as their workplace. The general lesson is that leaders should discover what is distinctive about their own team rather than copying what other enterprises do. The move is from a single concrete example to a transferable principle about retention and engagement.
points: Retention and service quality at an hourly-wage company were driven by investing in workers' children's education rather than by standard perks.
The programs include tutoring, rewards for good grades and one of the most lucrative tuition reimbursement packages in any industry.
Investing in what a person values most signals how much they matter and produces an unusual bond.
Leaders who copy the norms of other enterprises lose the creative insight needed to invent programs that fit their own team.
quotes: For more than a decade, she has run a holding company with businesses in the petroleum, convenience store, and healthcare sectors. With over 7,000 employees, most of whom are hourly workers, she has found a surprisingly refreshing way to increase employee retention and motivate people to provide the best service possible to their many customers.

As the CEO of Flying J travel centers and Maverik convenience stores, Maggelet has created the ultimate incentive for hourly workers to remain loyal to the company and the important services they provide. She has developed several programs to invest in the education of the workers’ children.

The FJ Management company provides tutors for the children of those that work at their centers and stores, pays for good grades for those that have children in school, and offers one of the most lucrative tuition reimbursement programs in any industry for both the workers and their offspring. Maggelet knows what every great leader should. Understanding what really matters to people and investing in it creates an unusual bond.

Few parents hold anything more valuable than their children and their educational futures. By creating a host of programs that invest in the children of those who work for the company, the leadership team at FJ Management tells their employees how much they — and their children — matter.
Team members who work at the company know instantly this is not like any other opportunity. So, they dig in and make it their workplace.

Too many leaders allow the norms of what other enterprises do to sap the creative insight needed to invent programs that change team member engagement. Every team and workplace is somewhat unique. Great leaders learn what matters most to their team members and invest in it.
